rows.answer: Assuming "best" means on-time delivery rate, Pioneer Carriers 98 LLC ranks first with 92.94% of its 170 delivered loads on time, followed closely by Big River Hauling Co. (92.82% on 195 loads) and Eagle Transit 97 LLC (92.66% on 177). Across the 40 carriers with at least 30 delivered loads, the overall on-time rate is 88.48%, and the range runs from 46.3% at the weakest to 92.94% at the top. Pioneer Carriers 98 LLC's linehaul margin is 14.71%, so it also pays well relative to the other top carriers. If you meant a different measure, such as margin or volume, I can rerun the ranking on that.
sql:
WITH d AS (
  SELECT l.carrier_id,
         COUNT(*) AS delivered_loads,
         SUM(CASE WHEN l.delivery_actual <= l.delivery_appt THEN 1 ELSE 0 END) AS on_time_loads,
         SUM(l.shipper_rate - l.carrier_cost) AS total_margin,
         SUM(l.shipper_rate) AS total_rate
  FROM loads l
  WHERE l.status = 'Delivered' AND l.carrier_id IS NOT NULL
  GROUP BY l.carrier_id
  HAVING COUNT(*) >= 30
)
SELECT c.name AS carrier,
       d.delivered_loads,
       ROUND(100.0 * d.on_time_loads / d.delivered_loads, 2) AS on_time_pct,
       ROUND(100.0 * d.total_margin / d.total_rate, 2) AS margin_pct,
       RANK() OVER (ORDER BY 1.0 * d.on_time_loads / d.delivered_loads DESC) AS on_time_rank
FROM d JOIN carriers c ON c.carrier_id = d.carrier_id
ORDER BY on_time_pct DESC, delivered_loads DESC
LIMIT 15

WITH d AS (
  SELECT carrier_id, COUNT(*) AS n,
         SUM(CASE WHEN delivery_actual <= delivery_appt THEN 1 ELSE 0 END) AS ot
  FROM loads WHERE status='Delivered' AND carrier_id IS NOT NULL
  GROUP BY carrier_id HAVING COUNT(*) >= 30
)
SELECT COUNT(*) AS carriers_qualifying,
       ROUND(100.0*SUM(ot)/SUM(n),2) AS overall_on_time_pct,
       ROUND(100.0*MIN(1.0*ot/n),2) AS worst_on_time_pct,
       ROUND(100.0*MAX(1.0*ot/n),2) AS best_on_time_pct
FROM d
LIMIT 200

rows.answer: Assuming you mean margin on delivered loads by pickup month, margin has held steady at about 14.4–14.6% from April through August, then dropped to 13.81% in September, the lowest month of the period. Average margin per load fell from $262.25 in August to $246.13 in September. The query doesn't break this down by lane or carrier, so I can't say yet what drove the September drop.
sql:
SELECT strftime('%Y-%m', pickup_appt) AS month,
       COUNT(*) AS delivered_loads,
       ROUND(SUM(shipper_rate), 2) AS revenue,
       ROUND(SUM(shipper_rate - carrier_cost), 2) AS margin,
       ROUND(100.0 * SUM(shipper_rate - carrier_cost) / SUM(shipper_rate), 2) AS margin_pct,
       ROUND(AVG(shipper_rate - carrier_cost), 2) AS avg_margin_per_load
FROM loads
WHERE status = 'Delivered'
GROUP BY month
ORDER BY month
LIMIT 200

rows.answer: Delivered loads from Memphis, TN to Atlanta, GA averaged 14.12 hours in transit from actual pickup to actual delivery. That is across 497 loads, with a range of 7.13 to 44.05 hours.
sql:
SELECT COUNT(*) AS delivered_loads,
       ROUND(AVG((julianday(delivery_actual) - julianday(pickup_actual)) * 24), 2) AS avg_transit_hours,
       ROUND(MIN((julianday(delivery_actual) - julianday(pickup_actual)) * 24), 2) AS min_transit_hours,
       ROUND(MAX((julianday(delivery_actual) - julianday(pickup_actual)) * 24), 2) AS max_transit_hours
FROM loads
WHERE status = 'Delivered'
  AND UPPER(TRIM(origin_city)) = 'MEMPHIS' AND UPPER(TRIM(origin_state)) = 'TN'
  AND UPPER(TRIM(dest_city)) = 'ATLANTA' AND UPPER(TRIM(dest_state)) = 'GA'
  AND pickup_actual IS NOT NULL AND delivery_actual IS NOT NULL
LIMIT 200

rows.answer: Bluegrass Haulers LLC arrived late on 53.7% of its delivered loads: 87 of 162 delivered loads (Apr–Sep 2026) had an actual delivery after the appointment time. Loads without both an appointment and an actual delivery time were excluded from the count.
sql:
WITH c AS (
  SELECT carrier_id, name FROM carriers WHERE name = 'Bluegrass Haulers LLC'
),
d AS (
  SELECT l.load_id, l.delivery_appt, l.delivery_actual, c.name
  FROM loads l JOIN c ON l.carrier_id = c.carrier_id
  WHERE l.status = 'Delivered' AND l.delivery_actual IS NOT NULL AND l.delivery_appt IS NOT NULL
)
SELECT name,
  COUNT(load_id) AS delivered_loads,
  SUM(CASE WHEN delivery_actual > delivery_appt THEN 1 ELSE 0 END) AS late_loads,
  ROUND(100.0 * SUM(CASE WHEN delivery_actual > delivery_appt THEN 1 ELSE 0 END) / COUNT(load_id), 2) AS late_pct
FROM d
GROUP BY name
LIMIT 200

Bluegrass Haulers LLC has 87 late deliveries out of 162 delivered loads, a 53.7% late rate, and the late ones averaged 4.42 hours past appointment. sql:
WITH c AS (
  SELECT carrier_id, name FROM carriers WHERE name = 'Bluegrass Haulers LLC'
),
d AS (
  SELECT l.load_id, l.origin_city, l.origin_state, l.dest_city, l.dest_state,
         l.delivery_appt, l.delivery_actual,
         CASE WHEN l.delivery_actual > l.delivery_appt THEN 1 ELSE 0 END AS is_late
  FROM loads l
  JOIN c ON l.carrier_id = c.carrier_id
  WHERE l.status = 'Delivered'
)
SELECT
  (SELECT COUNT(*) FROM c) AS matching_carriers,
  COUNT(*) AS delivered_loads,
  SUM(is_late) AS late_loads,
  ROUND(100.0 * SUM(is_late) / COUNT(*), 2) AS late_pct,
  ROUND(AVG(CASE WHEN is_late = 1 THEN (julianday(delivery_actual) - julianday(delivery_appt)) * 24 END), 2) AS avg_hours_late_when_late
FROM d
LIMIT 200

Harbor Foods DC - Atlanta (GA) had the most detention charges with a delivered-facility link in September 2026: 10 charges totaling $2,343.75, averaging $234.38. That is the only facility with a link, though, and it covers just 10 of the 240 detention charges booked that month ($52,818.75 total). The other 230 charges have no delivery facility on the load, so this answer is not a complete ranking. Assuming "in September" means the accessorial's created date, the facility can only be identified for the few loads where delivery_facility_id is populated.
sql:
WITH det AS (
  SELECT a.accessorial_id, a.amount, l.delivery_facility_id
  FROM accessorials a
  JOIN loads l ON l.load_id = a.load_id
  WHERE a.type = 'Detention'
    AND strftime('%Y-%m', a.created_at) = '2026-09'
)
SELECT f.facility_id, f.name, f.city, f.state,
       COUNT(*) AS detention_charges,
       ROUND(SUM(d.amount), 2) AS total_detention,
       ROUND(AVG(d.amount), 2) AS avg_detention
FROM det d
JOIN facilities f ON f.facility_id = d.delivery_facility_id
GROUP BY f.facility_id, f.name, f.city, f.state
ORDER BY total_detention DESC
LIMIT 10

SELECT COUNT(*) AS detention_charges_total,
       SUM(CASE WHEN l.delivery_facility_id IS NULL THEN 1 ELSE 0 END) AS no_delivery_facility,
       ROUND(SUM(a.amount), 2) AS total_amount_all
FROM accessorials a
JOIN loads l ON l.load_id = a.load_id
WHERE a.type = 'Detention'
  AND strftime('%Y-%m', a.created_at) = '2026-09'
LIMIT 200

rows.answer: Assuming "cargo insurance" means the `cargo_insurance_limit` on each carrier record, 779 of our 1,800 carriers (43.28%) carry less than $250,000 in cargo coverage. All 1,800 carriers have a numeric limit on file, with none missing, so the count is complete.

WITH d AS (
  SELECT l.carrier_id,
         COUNT(*) AS delivered_loads,
         SUM(CASE WHEN julianday(l.delivery_actual) > julianday(l.delivery_appt) THEN 1 ELSE 0 END) AS late_loads
  FROM loads l
  WHERE l.status = 'Delivered'
    AND l.delivery_actual IS NOT NULL

)

       d.delivered_loads,
       d.late_loads,
       ROUND(100.0 * (d.delivered_loads - d.late_loads) / d.delivered_loads, 2) AS on_time_pct
FROM d
JOIN carriers c ON c.carrier_id = d.carrier_id
ORDER BY on_time_pct ASC, d.delivered_loads DESC
LIMIT 5
